parent_prompt:
You receive 5 images. Image 1 is the LAYOUT SKETCH of the finished 1920x1080 game screen: a crude flat-colour blocking that fixes the exact composition - camera, horizon, wall and floor lines, and the position, size and outline of every object. Repaint image 1 into a finished painting: keep every line and every block exactly where it is and exactly as large as it is, paint each block as the object described below, do not move, enlarge, shrink, add or remove anything, and leave no flat colour areas or hard geometric edges. Images 2-4 are photos of the real place (geography, architecture, materials and real details to paint from; they are references only, do not copy their camera, cars, people, signs or weather). Image 5 is a finished background painting from our game: use it ONLY as the reference for the painting technique (brushwork, palette, edge softness, level of detail, line quality); do not copy anything from its scene.

Place: the Svantnerova tram stop on M. Schneidra-Trnavskeho street in Bratislava-Dubravka (Slovakia), seen from its south-west platform, looking north-west along the platform and up the street. The street is a wide dual carriageway with the double tram track between the carriageways: from left to right the west carriageway (asphalt), the platform with the shelter, the tram track bed, a red railing, the east carriageway, then on the right a low bluish medical centre with a long 8-storey prefabricated panel block with red-orange balconies behind it. In the distance the street, the tracks and the lamp posts climb a gentle hill and disappear over its crest among trees. Image 2 is a recent photo of this very street taken from the west carriageway (use it for the real look of the place: the low two-storey medical centre with its long white ribbon windows and its blue-grey mosaic-tiled walls, the panel block with the red-orange balconies behind it, the birches and lindens, the wide street with the tracks beside the road; do NOT copy its camera, its modern concrete barriers, its cars or its signs). Image 3 is a 1993 photo of a red-cream Tatra T3 tram on an old track bed of big grey concrete panels with grooved rails set into them (use it for the 1990s track bed and the tram's shape and livery only; no number, no route text, no driver). Image 4 is another red-cream Tatra T3 in Dubravka (shape and colours only).

Brief: the Dubravka tram stop in June 1995, early on a sunny summer morning: warm low morning sunlight from the right behind the camera, long soft shadows falling forward to the left, fresh green lindens and birches. The ORIGINAL 1980s stop: a long shelter made of brown-painted (dark burgundy-brown) steel tubes bent into arches - each arch rises from the platform at the back, curves over the top and comes down to the platform at the front - with a solid brown back wall of vertical boards along the road side and a translucent light-blue curved plastic roof; a wooden slat bench along the inside of the back wall; the platform paved with big grey concrete slabs, with a light, almost white edge strip along the track. The track bed of BOTH tracks is the old one: big grey concrete panels with the grooved rails set flush into them, thin grass growing in the joints, no ballast and no sleepers. A red steel-tube railing runs along the far side of the track bed, between the tracks and the east carriageway. An old red-cream Tatra T3 tram (cream upper body, window band and roof edge, red lower body, round headlights, a diamond pantograph raised to the wire) stands at the platform with its doors closed; its route box above the windscreen is blank, no number, no destination text. Tall rust-red street lamp posts with curved arms line both outer edges of the street, with span wires across carrying the overhead contact wires. 1995 details: a colourful 1990s advertising poster with abstract shapes (no lettering) in the first bay of the shelter's back wall, a paper timetable in a glazed case, no electronic display anywhere, no tactile paving.

Camera: eye level about 2 m above the platform, looking along the platform; the horizon is at y 400 and the flat near part of the track vanishes at x ~873, but from about 20 m ahead the street rises: the far roads, rails and lamp posts climb gently and reach the crest at about y 333, so the far part of the street is seen going uphill. Keep this exact geometry from the sketch: the platform from the bottom edge to the far end, its light edge strip from x 1324-1474 at the bottom edge receding towards the vanishing point, the near rails from (1632, 1080) and (1920, 1000), the shelter's back wall from x 279 (near end, y 352-777) receding to x ~800, the front tubes standing at x 636 (near) and further back, the stop post standing at x 678 with its foot at y 817 and the clock on top centred at (678, 147), the tram's front face at x 1111-1398, y 304-628, the medical centre's long facade from x 1167 (far end) to x 1711 (near corner, y 151-465) and its end wall right of it, the red-balcony panel slab above it at the top right.

What the sketch blocks are, left to right: at the far left the west carriageway (asphalt) beside the platform, a green verge with big lindens and a tall 12-storey point tower with yellow-orange balconies beyond it; at the near left the gap in the low concrete road-side wall where a short ramp goes down to the zebra crossing (the wall's end at the ramp has a chipped-off corner); the long brown tube shelter with its solid brown back wall, the translucent blue roof, the poster in the first bay and the bench; the stop post with the clock on top, a small stop plate and the timetable case; the platform; the light edge strip; the two tracks in their concrete-panel bed; the red-cream tram on the near track; the red railing; the east carriageway with a white dashed centre line; the low bluish medical centre (two storeys, flat roof with a white edge, two long white ribbon-window bands on the far part, the near end clad in blue-grey mosaic tiles); a white birch in front of it; behind it the long 8-storey panel slab with red-orange balcony bands; the tall rust-red lamp posts; far away in the middle the crest of the street with trees and a few distant white panel towers; clear blue sky with a few small clouds.

Interactive props - each painted clearly inside its block, the same size as its block, easy to recognise at a glance:
1. the block of the layout sketch at x 614-742, y 440-580 of the 1920x1080 frame (32-39 % from the left, 41-54 % from the top): the glazed timetable case on the grey stop post, white paper inside printed with neat columns of illegible tiny print (no digits); above it on the post a small white stop plate with a red border and a simple tram pictogram (no words), and on top of the post a round clock with a polished brass frame and a white dial with black hour ticks (no numerals), the hands showing about five past eight.
2. the block of the layout sketch at x 396-606, y 504-708 of the 1920x1080 frame (21-32 % from the left, 47-66 % from the top): the wooden slat bench inside the shelter along the back wall, seat and backrest of warm brown slats on black steel legs; two small pink chewing-gum blobs stuck under the front edge of the seat.
the area of the layout sketch at x 0-250, y 760-960 of the 1920x1080 frame (0-13 % from the left, 70-89 % from the top) is the gap in the low road-side wall at the near left where a short concrete ramp leads down to the west carriageway and the zebra crossing (towards the school); the end of the low concrete wall right at the ramp has a small chipped-off corner. the area of the layout sketch at x 780-1020, y 430-642 of the 1920x1080 frame (41-53 % from the left, 40-59 % from the top) is the far end of the platform beyond the shelter. the area of the layout sketch at x 1111-1398, y 304-628 of the 1920x1080 frame (58-73 % from the left, 28-58 % from the top) is the tram itself, standing at the platform.

Walkable floor: the open platform in front of the shelter and to the right of it (within the band at x 0-1262, y 664-1015 of the 1920x1080 frame (0-66 % from the left, 61-94 % from the top), except the shelter, its tubes and the stop post at its left edge, which stay exactly as in the sketch) is grey concrete slabs - one continuous flat surface with no kerb, step, edge or change of material inside it, and nothing else standing on it: no bins, no extra posts, no benches, no bags, no people. Only morning light, long shadows and fine joints between the slabs.
This room has no NPC zones.
Fixed architectural anchor 'curb' at x 231, y 784. Fixed architectural anchor 'track_line' at x 1525, y 774. Fixed architectural anchor 'clock_frame' at x 678, y 147.

Fiction rules: a generic Dubravka stop: no stop name, no transport-company logos, no line numbers, no route or destination text, no readable timetable; no signs, lettering or brands on the medical centre or anywhere else (no petrol-station or shop signs, no billboards); no car number plates. No people anywhere (no driver or passengers visible in the tram - its windows reflect the sky), no animals, no cars on the roads. Any paper shows only illegible scribbles, no digits.

The layout sketch is a blocking aid only: paint over all of it. Do NOT draw frames, borders, outlines or boxes around objects, and keep no flat colour block. The finished picture contains no UI, no captions, no text except what is asked for above, no watermark and no people or animals unless stated above.
